newsitem.title: USA: Long-term US fiscal stability key, Greenspan says.
newsitem.headline: Long-term US fiscal stability key, Greenspan says.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Aaln Greenspan said on Tuesday that any balanced budget agreement should be structured so as to ensure fiscal stability in the long-run.
In that regard, he told the House Budget Committee that America's long-term budget woes cannot be solved by raising taxes alone.
Spending must be curbed, especially in the Medicare and Medicaid health programs for the elderly and the poor, he said.
Greenspan said the Fed would not adjust monetary policy in direct reponse to any change in fiscal policy.
Instead, he suggested, the central bank would take its cue from any impact that such a budget change would have on financial markets and the economy.
